exact_statement: There exists an absolute C such that for every n and every f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, H_2(p_f) <= C I(f), where p_f(S)=fhat(S)^2, H_2(p_f)=sum_S p_f(S) log_2(1/p_f(S)), I(f)=sum_S |S|p_f(S), and fhat(S)=E_uniform[f(x) product_{i in S} x_i].
source_quote: there is a universal constant C such that H[fb2] ≤ C · I[f] holds for all Boolean-valued functions f.
